answers.drew: I always loved to write, but when I lost an entire manuscript on a hard drive in 3rd grade. It took a personal challenge to shoot an ambitious 28 minute short film (for Pride Month in 6 weeks from concept to distribution), over a decade later, for me to fall back in love with writing again. And that, I did. I graduating with an MFA in Screenwriting from UT Austin in 3 weeks!
answers.seeking: I'm looking to connect with fellow writers, execs, directors, producers, content creators, animators,  and below-the-line crew members! I'm looking to grow with a cohort of peers.
answers.inspiration:
I personally enjoy everything Gina Prince-Blythwood does, but my greatest inspiration is my mother. She was the first to believe in me and my writing. I typically write anything monsters and magic, folklore and myths, fairy tales and cryptids. I am a heavy genre storyteller who writes about the parentified child who reclaims stolen legacies and defines their own destinies. This is because I watched three generations of women before me doing exactly that.

As an early diagnosed, openly disabled creative and recovering overachiever, I am endlessly inspired by the dyslexia and neurodivergent creatives who have paved this path before me. I have a communication disorder and have become particularly skilled in language and communication — not in spite of my disability but because of living with it. As a twice-exceptional (gifted and disabled), queer, Black storyteller from humble beginnings who was hospitalized for depression at the age of 8, my outlook on life shifted to something more based in gratitude, reluctant optimism, and endless hope.
